newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rheinmetall, Badenwerk, Bae buy out STN Atlas.
newsitem.headline: Rheinmetall, Badenwerk, Bae buy out STN Atlas.

text.p: A consortium of Rheinmetall AG, Badenwerk AG and British Aerospace on Thursday signed a contract with the official receiver to buy STN Atlas, defence unit of bankrupt Bremer Vulkan AG.

Rheinmetall said in a news release that it and Badenwerk would take 51 percent of STN Atlas and BAe the remaining 49 percent. The sale price of STN Atlas was 550 million marks ($367.4 million). The deal is subject to cartel office approval.
Rheinmetall will be in executive control over STN Atlas, which will receive 250 million marks out of the sale price in order to strengthen its capital base.
Rheinmetall chief executive Hans Brauner dismissed press reports that STN Atlas -- the only profitable unit in the defunct Bremer Vulkan shipyard group -- would be broken up.

"STN Atlas Elektronik should be kept in one piece; a breakup, which has been misleadingly discussed and written about, is in no way under consideration," Brauner said, adding that STN's Bremen base would be kept.
Brauner added that he saw the acquisition of STN Atlas as a contribution to the consolidation process going on in the German defence industry, adding that he thought further talks were needed.

With the sale, receiver Jobst Wellensiek has stuck to his timetable to dispose of STN Atlas by the end of this year despite official pressure to keep the company from going outright to a foreign buyer.
